source_text: Οὔπω οἱ ὀδόντες τῷ σκύλακι, καὶ ὅμως διὰ τοῦ στόματος ἀμύνεται τὸν λυπήσαντα. Οὔπω τὰ κέρατα τῷ μόσχῳ, καὶ οἶδε ποῦ τὰ ὅπλα αὐτῷ ἐμφυήσεται. Ταῦτα ἀπόδειξιν ἔχει τοῦ ἀδιδάκτους εἶναι τὰς φύσεις ἁπάντων, καὶ μηδὲν εἶναι ἄτακτον μηδὲ ἀόριστον ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν, ἀλλὰ πάντα ἴχνη φέρειν τῆς τοῦ ποιήσαντος σοφίας, ἐν ἑαυτοῖς δεικνύντα ὅτι ἐμπαράσκευα πρὸς τὴν φυλακὴν τῆς οἰκείας αὐτῶν σωτηρίας παρήχθη. Λόγου μὲν ἄμοιρος ὁ κύων, ἰσοδυναμοῦσαν δὲ ὅμως τῷ λόγῳ αἴσθησιν ἔχει. Ἃ γὰρ οἱ κατὰ πολλὴν σχολὴν τοῦ βίου καθεζόμενοι μόλις ἐξεῦρον οἱ τοῦ κόσμου σοφοὶ, τὰς τῶν συλλογισμῶν λέγω πλοκὰς, ταῦτα δείκνυται παρὰ τῆς φύσεως ὁ κύων πεπαιδευμένος. Τὸ γὰρ ἴχνος τοῦ θηρίου διερευνώμενος, ἐπειδὰν εὕρῃ αὐτὸ πολυτρόπως σχιζόμενον, τὰς ἑκασταχοῦ φερούσας ἐκτροπὰς ἐπελθὼν, μονονουχὶ τὴν συλλογιστικὴν φωνὴν ἀφίησι δι' ὧν πράσσει· ἢ τήνδε, φησὶν, ἐτράπη τὸ θηρίον, ἢ τήνδε, ἢ ἐπὶ τόδε τὸ μέρος· ἀλλὰ μὴν οὔτε τήνδε, οὔτε τήνδε, λειπόμενόν ἐστι τῇδε ὡρμῆσθαι αὐτό· καὶ οὕτως τῇ ἀναιρέσει τῶν ψευδῶν εὑρίσκει τὸ ἀληθές. Τί περισσότερον ποιοῦσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τῶν διαγραμμάτων σεμνῶς καθεζόμενοι, καὶ τὴν κόνιν καταχαράσσοντες, τριῶν προτάσεων ἀναιροῦντες τὰς δύο, καὶ ἐν τῇ λειπομένῃ τὸ ἀληθὲς ἐξευρίσκοντες; Τὸ δὲ μνημονικὸν τῆς χάριτος τοῦ ζῴου, τίνα τῶν ἀχαρίστων πρὸς εὐεργέτας οὐ καταισχύνει; Ὅπου γε καὶ φονευθεῖσι δεσπόταις κατ' ἐρημίαν, πολλοὶ τῶν κυνῶν ἐπαποθανόντες μνημονεύονται. Ἤδη δέ τινες ἐπὶ θερμῷ τῷ πάθει καὶ ὁδηγοὶ τοῖς ἐκζητοῦσι τοὺς φονέας ἐγένοντο, καὶ ὑπὸ τὴν δίκην ἀχθῆναι τοὺς κακούργους ἐποίησαν. Τί εἴπωσιν οἱ τὸν ποιήσαντα αὐτοὺς καὶ τρέφοντα Κύριον οὐ μόνον οὐκ ἀγαπῶντες, ἀλλὰ καὶ φίλοις κεχρημένοι τοῖς λαλοῦσι κατὰ τοῦ Θεοῦ ἀδικίαν, καὶ τῆς αὐτῆς αὐτοῖς τραπέζης μετέχοντες, καὶ παρ' αὐτὴν τὴν τροφὴν τῶν κατὰ τοῦ τρέφοντος βλασφημιῶν ἀνεχόμενοι; 9.5 Ἀλλ' ἐπὶ τὴν θεωρίαν τῆς κτίσεως ἐπανίωμεν. Τὰ εὐαλωτότερα τῶν ζῴων, πολυγονώτερα. Διὰ τοῦτο πολυτόκοι λαγωοὶ, καὶ αἶγες ἄγριαι, καὶ πρόβατα ἄγρια διδυμοτόκα, ἵνα μὴ ἐπιλείπῃ τὸ γένος ὑπὸ τῶν ὠμοβόρων ἐκδαπανώμενον. Τὰ δὲ φθαρτικὰ τῶν ἄλλων, ὀλιγοτόκα. Ὅθεν λέοντος ἑνὸς μόλις ἡ λέαινα μήτηρ γίνεται. Ταῖς γὰρ ἀκμαῖς τῶν ὀνύχων διασπαράξας τὴν μήτραν, οὕτω πρόεισιν, ὥς φασι· καὶ ἔχιδναι τὰς μήτρας ἐκφαγοῦσαι προέρχονται, πρέποντας τῇ γεννησαμένῃ τοὺς μισθοὺς ἐκτιννύουσαι. Οὕτως οὐδὲν ἀπρονόητον ἐν τοῖς οὖσιν, οὐδὲ τῆς ἐπιβαλούσης αὐτοῖς ἐπιμελείας ἄμοιρα. Κἂν αὐτὰ τὰ μέλη τῶν ζῴων καταμάθῃς, εὑρήσεις ὅτι οὔτε περιττόν τι ὁ κτίσας προσέθηκεν, οὔτε ἀφεῖλε τῶν ἀναγκαίων. Τοῖς σαρκοφάγοις ζῴοις ὀξεῖς τοὺς ὀδόντας ἐνήρμοσε· τοιούτων γὰρ ἦν χρεία πρὸς τὸ τῆς τροφῆς εἶδος. Ἃ δὲ ἐξ ἡμισείας ὥπλισται τοῖς ὀδοῦσι, πολλαῖς καὶ ποικίλαις ἀποθήκαις τῶν τροφῶν παρεσκεύασε. Διὰ γὰρ τὸ παρὰ τὴν πρώτην μὴ ἀρκούντως καταλεπτύνεσθαι τὴν τροφὴν, ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς τὸ καταποθὲν πάλιν ἀναπεμπάζεσθαι, ὥστε καταλεανθὲν τῷ μηρυκισμῷ προσοικειοῦσθαι τῷ τρεφομένῳ. Στόμαχοι καὶ ἐχῖνοι, καὶ κεκρύφαλοι, καὶ ἔνυστρα, οὐκ ἀργῶς ἔγκειται τῶν ζῴων τοῖς ἔχουσιν, ἀλλ' ἀναγκαίων χρείαν ἕκαστον ἐκπληροῖ. Μακρὸς ὁ τράχηλος τῆς καμήλου, ἵνα τοῖς ποσὶν ἐξισάζηται καὶ ἐφικνῆται τῆς βοτάνης ἐξ ἧς ἀποζῇ.
thought_title: Animal instincts and anatomy show the Creator's wisdom
orientation: Basil is still expounding the fifth day's creatures, arguing that even brute animals display innate wisdom and that every part of their bodies is fitted by the Creator for their needs.
pass_a_gloss: Not yet are the teeth in the puppy, and nevertheless through the mouth it defends itself against the one that hurt it. Not yet are the horns on the calf, and it knows where its weapons will grow. These things have proof that the natures of all things are untaught, and that nothing is disorderly nor undefined among the things that exist, but all things bear traces of the wisdom of the one who made them, showing in themselves that they were brought forth equipped beforehand for the guarding of their own safety. Of reason the dog is without share, but nevertheless it has a perception equal in power to reason. For what the wise men of the world, sitting down over much leisure of life, barely discovered—I mean the tangles of syllogisms—these things the dog is shown to have been taught by nature. For searching out the track of the beast, whenever it finds it split in many ways, having gone over the turnings that lead in each direction, it all but lets out the syllogistic voice through what it does: either this way, it says, the beast turned, or this way, or toward this part; but indeed neither this way nor this way; it remains that it rushed this way; and thus by the removal of the false things it finds the true thing. What more do those who sit solemnly over diagrams and scratch the dust do, removing two of three propositions and finding out the true thing in the one that remains? And the memory of gratitude of the animal, which of the ungrateful toward benefactors does it not put to shame? Since indeed even for masters murdered in a deserted place, many dogs are remembered as having died upon them. And already some in the heat of the suffering also became guides to those seeking the murderers, and made the criminals be brought under justice. What will they say, those who not only do not love the Lord who made them and nourishes them, but also have as friends those who speak injustice against God, and share the same table with them, and during the very food put up with blasphemies against the one who nourishes them? But let us return to the contemplation of creation. The more easily caught of the animals are more prolific. For this reason hares are many-bearing, and wild goats, and wild sheep are twin-bearing, so that the kind may not fail, being devoured by the flesh-eaters. But the destructive ones of others are few-bearing. Whence of one lion the lioness scarcely becomes mother. For with the points of its claws having torn apart the womb, thus it comes forth, as they say; and vipers come forth having eaten through the wombs, paying back fitting wages to the one that bore them. Thus nothing is unprovided-for among the things that exist, nor without share of the care that falls to them. And if you examine the very limbs of the animals, you will find that neither did the Creator add anything superfluous, nor did he take away any of the necessary things. For the flesh-eating animals he fitted with sharp teeth; for of such there was need for the kind of food. But those that are armed with teeth by half, he prepared with many and varied storehouses of foods. For because the food is not sufficiently broken down at the first, he gave them the swallowed thing to be chewed again, so that, ground down by the chewing of the cud, it may be made akin to the one being nourished. Stomachs and omasums, and net-like stomachs, and rennet stomachs, do not lie idle in the animals that have them, but each one fulfills the need of necessary things. Long is the neck of the camel, so that it may be equal to its feet and reach the grass from which it lives.

choices.why: πλοκή means a twisting or coiling; 'tangles' conveys the convoluted, intricate nature of syllogistic reasoning Basil means, avoiding the checker's objection to 'interweavings'.

choices.term: Στόμαχοι καὶ ἐχῖνοι, καὶ κεκρύφαλοι, καὶ ἔνυστρα
choices.english: Stomachs and omasums, and net-like stomachs, and rennet stomachs
choices.why: ἐχῖνοι here are the omasum (many-plies), so named for its sea-urchin-like internal folds; κεκρύφαλοι are the reticulum (net-like stomach); ἔνυστρα are the abomasum or rennet stomach. The order follows the source and keeps each term distinct.
rejected: Stomachs and hedgehogs, and net-like stomachs, and rennet stomachs
Stomachs and sea-urchins, and net-like stomachs, and rennet stomachs

choices.term: ἰσοδυναμοῦσαν δὲ ὅμως τῷ λόγῳ αἴσθησιν ἔχει
choices.english: nevertheless it has a perception equal in power to reason
choices.why: ἰσοδυναμοῦσαν means 'equal in power or force'; rendering it as 'equal in power to reason' preserves the comparative force Basil intends between animal perception and human reason.
rejected: a perception of equal force with reason

choices.english: it all but lets out the syllogistic voice
choices.why: μονονουχί means 'all but, almost'; the phrase captures Basil's point that the dog's behavior is tantamount to speaking a syllogism.
rejected: it almost utters the syllogistic voice
it nearly sends forth the syllogistic voice

choices.term: τῇ ἀναιρέσει τῶν ψευδῶν εὑρίσκει τὸ ἀληθές
choices.english: by the removal of the false things it finds the true thing
choices.why: ἀναίρεσις is the technical term for eliminating alternatives in a disjunctive syllogism; 'removal' keeps the logical force without importing modern logical jargon.
rejected: by the destruction of the false things
by the elimination of the false things

choices.why: ἐπαποθνῄσκω means 'to die upon or over'; the rendering preserves the image of dogs dying on their masters' bodies.

pass_b_english: The puppy does not yet have teeth, and yet it defends itself with its mouth against whatever hurts it. The calf does not yet have horns, and yet it knows where its weapons will grow in. These things prove that the natures of all creatures are untaught, and that nothing among existing things is disordered or undefined, but all things bear traces of the wisdom of their Maker, showing in themselves that they were brought forth equipped beforehand for the guarding of their own safety. The dog has no share in reason, but nevertheless it has a perception equal in power to reason. For what the wise men of the world, sitting down over the long leisure of their lives, have barely discovered—I mean the tangles of syllogisms—the dog is shown to have been taught by nature. For when it searches out the track of a wild animal and finds it split in many directions, it goes over the turnings that lead each way, and all but lets out the syllogistic voice through what it does: either the animal turned this way, it says, or that way, or toward this other part; but it did not turn this way or that way; therefore it remains that it rushed off that way. And so by the removal of the false things it finds the true thing. What more do those who sit solemnly over their diagrams and scratch in the dust accomplish, when they remove two of three propositions and discover the truth in the one that remains? And as for the memory of gratitude in this animal, which of the ungrateful toward their benefactors does it not put to shame? Many dogs are remembered for having died together with their masters when they were murdered in a deserted place. And some, while their grief was still fresh, even became guides to those searching for the murderers, and caused the criminals to be brought to trial. What will they say—those who not only do not love the Lord who made them and feeds them, but even treat as friends those who speak injustice against God, and share the same table with them, and put up with blasphemies against the One who feeds them right at the very meal? But let us return to the contemplation of creation. The animals that are more easily caught are more prolific. For this reason hares are prolific, and wild goats and wild sheep bear twins, so that the kind may not fail when it is consumed by flesh-eaters. But those that destroy others bear few young. Hence a lioness is barely the mother of one lion. For the lion tears the womb apart with the points of its claws and so comes forth, as they say; and vipers come forth by eating through the womb, paying back fitting wages to the mother that bore them. So nothing among existing things is without providence, nor without the care that belongs to it. And if you study the very limbs of animals, you will find that the Creator neither added anything superfluous nor removed anything necessary. To the flesh-eating animals he fitted sharp teeth; for such teeth were needed for the kind of food they eat. But those that are only half armed with teeth he prepared with many and varied storehouses of food. For because their food is not sufficiently ground up at the first pass, he gave them the ability to bring back up what they have swallowed, so that, after it is ground fine by chewing the cud, it may be assimilated to the one being nourished. Stomachs and omasums, and net-like stomachs, and rennet stomachs are not placed idly in the animals that have them, but each one fulfills the need of necessary functions. The neck of the camel is long, so that it may be equal to its feet and reach the grass on which it lives.

problems.why: ἐπαποθανόντες means 'died after/together with' (loyal dogs dying after their masters), not 'died upon'
problems.fix: many dogs are remembered for having died together with their masters

edits.old: Many dogs are remembered for having died upon their masters when they were murdered in a deserted place.
edits.new: Many dogs are remembered for having died together with their masters when they were murdered in a deserted place.

fixed: Changed 'died upon their masters' to 'died together with their masters' because ἐπαποθανόντες means 'died after/together with', not 'died upon'.

problems.source_quote: ὑπὸ τὴν δίκην ἀχθῆναι τοὺς κακούργους ἐποίησαν
problems.why: ἐποίησαν means 'caused/made' not 'became'; dogs caused criminals to be brought to trial, were not themselves agents of justice.
problems.fix: caused the criminals to be brought to trial

problems.quote: while the deed was still fresh
problems.why: πάθει means 'suffering/passion' (of the dogs' grief/love), not 'deed'; refers to their emotional state being still warm.
problems.fix: while their passion was still warm
problems.ruling: ἐπὶ θερμῷ τῷ πάθει = 'while passion still warm'; πάθει is emotion, not 'deed'—meaning changed.

edits.old: and brought the criminals to justice
edits.new: and caused the criminals to be brought to trial

edits.old: while the deed was still fresh
edits.new: while their passion was still warm

fixed: Changed 'brought the criminals to justice' to 'caused the criminals to be brought to trial' because the source 'ὑπὸ τὴν δίκην ἀχθῆναι τοὺς κακούργους ἐποίησαν' means the dogs caused the criminals to be brought to trial, not that they themselves brought them to justice.
Changed 'while the deed was still fresh' to 'while their passion was still warm' because the source 'ἐπὶ θερμῷ τῷ πάθει' refers to the dogs' emotional state (passion/suffering), not the deed.

problems.quote: while their passion was still warm
problems.why: πάθος here means 'suffering, grief, distress'—the dogs' grief for their dead masters. 'Passion' suggests anger or strong emotion generally, even sexual passion. Context is dogs mourning, not angry. 'Grief' or 'sorrow' needed.
problems.fix: while their grief was still fresh
problems.ruling: ἐπὶ θερμῷ τῷ πάθει: πάθος here is grief/distress over murdered masters; 'passion' misleads modern readers.

fixed: Changed 'while their passion was still warm' to 'while their grief was still fresh': πάθος here means 'suffering, grief, distress'—the dogs' grief for their dead masters, not anger or strong emotion.

dismissed.quote: he gave them the ability to bring back up what they have swallowed
dismissed.why: Missing 'again' (πάλιν); the ability is specifically to bring back up again what was swallowed, the repeated action of rumination.
dismissed.note: 'Bring back up' already carries the sense of πάλιν; the suggested fix is also bad English.
